chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Miskan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about one who bought a sheep and it had not been identified as such. He said: There is no problem with it, whether it was identified as such or it was not identified as such.

The correct way regarding this report is that we understand it to mean that the buyer had not identified it as such, while the seller mentioned that he had identified it as such. So he is believed in that, and it suffices for him. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.شَاةً: a sheep intended here in the context of sacrificial use
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem; it is permissible
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: it suffices for him and fulfills the requirement
key_terms.يُصَدِّقُهُ: he accepts his statement as truthful
key_terms.يُعَرِّفْ: to identify or designate it in the required manner

ai.seo_question: Is a sheep valid for sacrifice if the buyer did not personally identify or designate it beforehand?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on purchasing a sheep for sacrifice when the buyer himself did not perform the required prior designation. The report indicates permissibility, and the closing clarification explains that if the seller had already identified it appropriately, the buyer may rely on that and it is sufficient.
